---
title: "Resources: Reviewing a vendor risk assessment"
order: 37
---

Each link below was checked this session and loads.

- **[21 CFR 606.171 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/606.171)**
  — the full "Reporting of product deviations" section, including paragraph (a), this module's
  contrast clause: a party performing a manufacturing, holding, or distribution step under a blood
  establishment's control is reached directly by the regulation; a software vendor generally isn't.
  Local verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/606.171.md`.

- **[21 CFR 11.10 — Cornell Legal Information Institute](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/21/11.10)**
  — the full "Controls for closed systems" section, including the introductory sentence this module
  reuses: the obligation to control a system sits on "persons who use" it, not its vendor. Local
  verbatim copy: `sources/cfr/11.10.md`.

- **[GovInfo: Code of Federal Regulations](https://www.govinfo.gov/app/collection/cfr)**
  — the government's own dated, authenticated CFR collection. Use this when a citation needs to be
  tied to a specific published edition rather than the current rolling text Cornell's LII shows.

- **[AABB: Updated Quality Systems Essentials](https://www.aabb.org/standards-accreditation/standards/about-aabb-standards/updated-quality-systems-essentials)**
  — AABB's current landing page on the QSE (Quality System Essentials) structure, including
  Suppliers and Customers (QSE 4), the theme this module draws on for qualifying and managing a
  vendor. Use it as a starting point; see `sources/aabb/qse-framework.md` for what's confirmed and
  what still needs re-checking before citing a specific edition.

- **[AICPA & CIMA: System and Organization Controls (SOC) Suite of Services](https://www.aicpa-cima.com/resources/landing/system-and-organization-controls-soc-suite-of-services)**
  — the body that maintains the SOC 2 (System and Organization Controls 2) framework this module
  names but deliberately doesn't teach the mechanics of. Use it only for what a SOC 2 report *is*,
  as background for later — reading what a specific report actually says is
  `vendor-and-third-party-risk-management`'s job, not this module's.

- **[09 Module 9 Supplier Management and Cloud Systems](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rQC-Wqzxvhc)**
  (WhitehallTraining, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A general
  GxP-training overview of supplier management and cloud systems; not blood-specific and not an
  FDA or AABB source, so use it for the general shape of IT supplier assessment only. Its video
  description could not be read, so the lesson claims only what the title says. Verified
  embeddable via YouTube oEmbed on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[FDA: Contract Manufacturing Arrangements for Drugs: Quality Agreements](https://www.fda.gov/regulatory-information/search-fda-guidance-documents/contract-manufacturing-arrangements-drugs-quality-agreements)**
  — FDA's guidance on written quality agreements that divide responsibilities between an owner
  and a contracted party. It is a drug-industry (CGMP) guidance, not a blood or software one, but
  it shows how a regulator expects duties like change notification to be written down rather than
  assumed — the same instinct behind this lesson's "put it in the contract, not in good faith."
  Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[ISPE: GAMP 5 Guide, 2nd Edition](https://ispe.org/publications/guidance-documents/gamp-5-guide-2nd-edition)**
  — the publisher's page for the industry's best-known guide to risk-based management of GxP
  computerized systems, including how to assess and manage software suppliers. The guide itself is
  a paid publication; read this page to know what it covers and where it fits, not for the
  content. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management](https://csrc.nist.gov/projects/cyber-supply-chain-risk-management)**
  — NIST's project page on managing risk from suppliers and third parties. It speaks to the
  security lens this lesson says needs its own owner, separate from the quality signature. It is
  general (not GMP or blood-specific). Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[European Commission: EudraLex Volume 4 (EU GMP guidelines)](https://health.ec.europa.eu/medicinal-products/eudralex/eudralex-volume-4_en)**
  — the EU's GMP collection, which includes Annex 11 on computerised systems and Chapter 7 on
  outsourced activities. It is EU rules for medicinal products, not FDA or blood-bank law; read it
  as a worked comparison for how another regulator expects suppliers of computerized systems to be
  controlled. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
